I went offline for 7 days and left Grok Bot one message: run my company while I'm away and only ask me about money.

It spun up 8 bots, gave each one a corner of the business and put them all in orbit around itself.

Then it just worked.

Day 1: the inbox bot took 212 emails down to 0 and kept 9 for me.

Day 2: the haggle bot found 18 seats we were paying for and nobody used, saving $84 a month, and it asked before cancelling, so I tapped yes from a beach.

Day 3: the pipeline bot caught 3 deals going cold and followed up before they died, while the bug bot turned an iOS crash into a failing test and a PR.

Day 4: the invoice bot chased 4 late clients and 2 of them paid $3,200.

Day 5: the account bot flagged 2 customers about to churn and wrote the save plan.

Day 7: Chief of Staff sent me one brief with the 6 things that actually mattered this week.

In total it saved and collected $4,630, I opened 0 chats and tapped approve 3 times.

The part people miss is that none of them go rogue, because every bot stops at a draft and anything that costs money waits for your tap.

I didn't build any of this from scratch, since most of these bots are already sitting in the Grok Bot marketplace and take one tap to add.

If you left tomorrow for a week, which bot would you hire first?

The film is my render.

I've been liking @grokbot so far, but there are some things that could be improved:

1. No quick scroll or quick search within chat (as far as I can tell)
2. Checking for updates doesn't give an affirmative toast message or any indicator within the app to ensure that I'm up to date. 

Separately, I would love to see event trigger automation and SMS capability added soon. Currently, ChatGPT Dot can start a task when a new Gmail message arrives, rather than waiting for the next scheduled inbox check, and it just added SMS capability, with limitations. 

Overall, excited to see where Grok Bot goes from here!
